title: NY State Assembly · District 87
area: Southeast Bronx, including Parkchester, Castle Hill, Van Nest, West Farms, Unionport and Westchester Square.

context.text: Incumbent Karines Reyes defeated Zakir Choudhury 71.6%-28.1% in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary. Choudhury remains on the November ballot on the People First Party line, a separate ballot line he also secured. Zenobia Merced-Bonilla advanced unopposed on the Conservative Party line.

candidates.name: Karines Reyes

summary.text: Karines Reyes is the Democratic and Working Families Party nominee for re-election in NY Assembly District 87, a seat she has held since January 2019. A registered nurse who served on a hospital union executive committee, she was first elected in 2018 and serves on the Codes, Health, Higher Education, Labor, Alcoholism and Drug Abuse, and Social Services committees. Her campaign website says she is focused on affordable healthcare, affordable housing and protecting immigrant families.

background.text: Born in the Los Minas neighborhood of Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic; her family moved to Carolina, Puerto Rico in her early childhood, and she immigrated to the United States with her mother at age 6, settling in Corona, Queens.

Attended the High School of Art and Design, graduating with honors, then studied communications at CUNY Baruch College; Ballotpedia lists an associate degree from Bronx Community College and a bachelor's degree from Baruch College. According to her official biography, she obtained her nursing degree by 2013.
Before nursing, worked at Mount Sinai Hospital in Health Information Management, for Aramark at Mount Sinai, and as an admissions coordinator in its Physical Therapy Department.

Began her nursing career at Montefiore Hospital on the in-patient oncology ward, earned a chemotherapy infusion certification and worked as an infusion nurse at the Eastchester Cancer Center; her official biography describes her as a registered nurse in the Oncology Department at Montefiore Einstein Hospital.

Served on the New York State Nurses Association (NYSNA) executive committee at Einstein Hospital as vice chair of the bargaining unit, and lobbied for safer nurse-to-patient ratios and single-payer health care in New York State.

Volunteered in Haiti as a student nurse after the earthquake and, after Hurricane Maria, served as a volunteer nurse with the first group of medical professionals deployed to Puerto Rico by New York State.

First elected to the Assembly on November 6, 2018 (Democratic and Working Families Party lines) in an open-seat race against Alpheaus Marcus (R) and Michael Dennis, and assumed office on January 1, 2019, succeeding Luis Sepúlveda; re-elected in 2020, 2022 and 2024.

Currently assigned to the Assembly's Alcoholism and Drug Abuse, Codes, Higher Education, Health, Labor and Social Services committees; says her work on the Health Committee informs her focus on healthcare access.

According to her campaign website, she worked with Assemblymember Amanda Septimo to secure the first state fund dedicated to Latino-serving organizations (the LUCHA Equity Fund) and fought for a federal RAISE grant to begin the process of capping the Cross Bronx Expressway.

priorities.text: Affordable education: fully funding Foundation Aid for K-12 schools and passing the New Deal for CUNY to provide tuition relief.
Affordable housing: protecting tenants and holding negligent landlords accountable.
Affordable healthcare: pushing for a healthcare system that works for patients over insurance companies.
Immigration justice: legislation to give immigrant residents stability, dignity and a fair shot.

positions.summary: As a nurse and member of the Assembly Health Committee, says she pushes for healthcare that works for patients rather than insurance companies, and championed Abortion Shield Laws protecting doctors and patients.
Says she works to protect tenants and hold negligent landlords accountable, and to push Albany to invest in housing that keeps working families in place.

Continues to lead the fight for the New York for All Act to protect immigrants regardless of status, and, with State Senator Andrew Gounardes, called for banning informal collusion between local agencies and ICE.
positions.quote: ICE's oppressive deportation dragnet is ripping apart families and killing...

positions.summary: Says she championed Abortion Shield Laws protecting doctors and patients involved in abortion care.
Championed the Retail Worker Safety Act and the Roadway Excavation Quality Assurance Act, guaranteeing prevailing wages for infrastructure workers, as part of her record protecting workers.

record.text: Championed the Retail Worker Safety Act, requiring panic buttons and violence-prevention plans for retail employees.
Championed the Roadway Excavation Quality Assurance Act, guaranteeing prevailing wages for infrastructure workers.
Secured passage of the New York State Fashion Workers Act, establishing basic labor protections for models and creatives.
Passed what her campaign calls the "Incorrigible Bill," removing offensive language from family and education law historically used to target girls of color.
Enacted the BIPOC Missing Women & Girls Task Force Bill, directing the state to address failures in missing-persons cases involving women of color.
Authored the NY HERO Act, establishing the first statewide airborne-infectious-disease workplace safety standard in the country.
Championed Abortion Shield Laws protecting doctors and patients, and a ban on toxic mercury in cosmetics.

Issued a joint statement with State Senator Andrew Gounardes calling for the full New York for All Act, opposing informal collusion between local agencies and ICE, following the state budget's ban on formal ICE agreements.

candidates.researchNotes: Reyes completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey in 2020, the most recent one on file (none for 2026); this file relies instead on her official Assembly biography and her campaign's own accomplishments/priorities pages for current information, since her sponsored-legislation table on Ballotpedia is rendered via JavaScript and was not accessible to this research tool.

candidates.name: Zenobia Merced-Bonilla

summary.text: Zenobia Merced-Bonilla is the Conservative Party nominee for NY Assembly District 87. She ran for New York City Council District 18 on the Conservative line in 2025, finishing third, and is described in a Bronx.com report as a Bronx Conservative Party district leader. Ballotpedia lists no prior elected office for her.

background.text: Ran for New York City Council District 18 on the Conservative Party line in the November 4, 2025 general election, finishing third behind incumbent Amanda Farias (D/WFP) and Shuvonkar Saha (R) with 582 votes (2.1%).

Described as a district leader in the Bronx Conservative Party in a Bronx.com report published January 31, 2026, which also says the party endorsed her for a different seat, New York State Senate District 34, before she appeared on the ballot for this Assembly seat.

priorities.text: Animal welfare, mental health, clean and safe streets, and public transportation, citing sanitation, disorder, and subway safety conditions as key concerns.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website or completed Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey was located for Merced-Bonilla. Background and priorities are drawn from her 2025 City Council candidacy and a Bronx.com report on a Bronx Conservative Party meeting reported on January 31, 2026, where she spoke about a State Senate District 34 campaign before she appeared on the ballot for this Assembly seat instead; no Assembly District 87-specific policy statements were found. No birthplace, education or employment information for her could be found in a loaded public source.

candidates.name: Zakir Choudhury

summary.text: Zakir Choudhury ran for the Democratic nomination for NY Assembly District 87 and lost to incumbent Karines Reyes 71.6%-28.1%; he remains on the November ballot on the People First Party line. His campaign website describes him as a first-generation American, licensed CPA, parent and community organizer, and he is running on accountability, affordability and public safety themes.

background.text: According to his campaign website, he is a first-generation American, a licensed CPA and a parent, who has lived and raised his family in the district for years.

His campaign website says his candidacy is shaped by decades of professional experience helping families, seniors and small businesses navigate financial challenges, and by work as a community organizer.
Lost the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary for this seat to incumbent Karines Reyes, 71.6%-28.1%; remains on the November ballot on the People First Party line.

priorities.text: Financial accountability and transparency: responsible budgeting, greater transparency in state spending, and reducing waste so tax dollars directly benefit District 87 residents.
Education and youth opportunities: fair and reliable school funding and expanded after-school and youth development programs.
Affordable living: reducing cost-of-living pressures, supporting affordable housing, and addressing rising energy and utility costs.
Public safety and community health: community-based safety programs and expanded access to mental health services.
Small business and local economy: support for entrepreneurs, local job creation, and reduced regulatory burdens.

positions.summary: Lists supporting affordable-housing initiatives among his areas of focus for addressing cost-of-living pressures in the district.

candidates.researchNotes: Choudhury has not completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and has no official record (Ballotpedia lists no prior office). His campaign website's "About" section contains placeholder text alongside genuine campaign content; only the material clearly specific to his candidacy (the "Vision for Change" issues page) was used here. Degrees and employer names appear only on voter-aggregator sites and were not used.
